title: A Pune IT Firm Just Made One of India's Biggest-Ever Overseas Tech Acquisitions. The Company It Bought Was Founded by Indians in Germany.
excerpt: Persistent Systems is paying $1.3 billion for Nagarro SE, creating a $2.9 billion AI-led engineering giant with 46,000 employees. The stock dropped 11% on the news.
body:
Persistent Systems, the Pune-based IT services firm, has announced an all-cash deal to acquire Germany's Nagarro SE for approximately $1.3 billion — one of the largest overseas acquisitions ever made by an Indian technology company. The combined entity will be a $2.9 billion AI-led engineering powerhouse with more than 46,000 employees across 40 countries.

The offer, made through a wholly-owned subsidiary called Galaxy Germany Holding SE, values Nagarro at €81 per share — a 140% premium over Nagarro's undisturbed closing price on June 25 and roughly 100% over its last close on Friday. Nagarro's management and supervisory board have said they intend to recommend the offer to shareholders.

## Two Indians Built This Company in Germany

The deal's most striking detail may be its origin story. Nagarro was founded in 1996 by two Indians — Vikram Sehgal and Manas Human (formerly Fuloria) — in Germany. Human, who remains CEO, also founded the Re-Imagining Higher Education Foundation that sponsors Plaksha University in Punjab. A German-listed company built by Indians is now being acquired by an Indian firm to create a global technology leader. The diaspora loop, in this case, closes neatly.

Human framed the deal in terms of the AI transformation wave. "With the AI revolution, we are entering an era that will reward companies like ours that already have a digital-, data- and AI-DNA," he said. "With the combined strengths of Persistent and Nagarro, we'll be able to deliver the complex intelligence transformation programs that our clients are increasingly demanding — at scale, across industries, and across the world."



> **""With the AI revolution, we are entering an era that will reward companies like ours that already have a digital-, data- and AI-DNA," he said."**


## What the Numbers Say

Persistent ended FY26 with $1.65 billion in revenue, up 17% year-on-year. Nagarro's growth has been slower — $999 million in 2025, up just 2.8%. The combined entity targets $5 billion in annual revenue by 2031.

The acquisition fundamentally changes Persistent's geographic mix. Europe currently accounts for just 9% of Persistent's revenue; after the deal closes, expected by March 2027, that rises to 22%. The combined group would earn roughly $750 million each from banking and telecom clients.

But analysts are not uniformly enthusiastic. UBS flagged the "excessive" valuations given Nagarro's relatively low growth profile. Bank of America maintained an "underperform" rating on Persistent, warning that integrating a company this large carries meaningful execution risk. On Monday, Persistent's stock fell as much as 11.2%, its largest intraday drop since April 2025.

## The India Angle

Persistent CEO Sandeep Kalra addressed the valuation concerns on a post-deal analyst call, arguing that Nagarro's recent slowdown reflects temporary distractions — including a failed attempt to take the company private last year — rather than structural weakness. He pointed to Nagarro's status as one of a select group of accredited OpenAI resellers and its specialised AI engineering team.

The deal adds verticals like industrials and automotive to Persistent's portfolio, which has traditionally been stronger in healthcare, financial services, and telecom. Management said the combined entity's margins would not fall below Persistent's current 15.6% operating margin, as the company plans cost synergies and will prune unprofitable "tail accounts" after the acquisition closes.

Of the 46,000 employees in the combined group, roughly 37,000 will be in India, 3,500 in North America, and 3,000 in Europe. For Indian tech workers, this is the kind of deal that creates career pathways between Pune and Munich, between Bangalore and Berlin — the sort of cross-border mobility the diaspora was built on.

## The Bigger Picture

The acquisition fits a pattern. Indian IT firms, flush with cash from years of dollar-denominated growth, are using overseas acquisitions to move up the value chain from legacy outsourcing into AI-led transformation. Persistent, once a mid-cap company focused on product engineering, is now positioning itself as a direct competitor to Accenture and Cognizant in the enterprise AI space.

Whether the premium is justified will depend on how quickly Persistent can accelerate Nagarro's growth and extract the margin synergies it has promised. But the ambition is unmistakable: India's technology sector is no longer content to be the world's back office. It wants to own the front door.

*Sources: Reuters, Livemint, The Hindu BusinessLine, Analytics Insight, Outlook Business*
